permutationLabel: Woman, CT-confirmed uncomplicated, no appendicolith (antibiotics-first candidate)
summary: 28-year-old woman, 20 h migratory RIF pain, urine hCG negative, US non-diagnostic, CT uncomplicated appendicitis without appendicolith; she asks to avoid surgery.

inputs.hpi: 20 hours of central abdominal pain moving to the right iliac fossa, anorexia and nausea. LMP 12 days ago, regular cycle. No vaginal discharge or bleeding. Urine pregnancy test negative in triage. She would like to avoid an operation if possible because she is travelling for work next week.
symptoms: migration of pain to the right iliac fossa

exam.abdomen: Tender right iliac fossa with mild localised guarding; no rebound, no mass. Rest of abdomen soft.

imaging.name: USS abdomen and pelvis
imaging.result: Appendix not visualised. Normal uterus and ovaries. No free fluid.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Uncomplicated acute appendicitis: appendix 9 mm with periappendiceal fat stranding. No appendicolith, no perforation, no abscess.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute appendicitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: CT-confirmed uncomplicated acute appendicitis without appendicolith. Discussed laparoscopic appendicectomy and antibiotics-first treatment.

socratesAnswers.lmp: 12 days ago, regular; urine hCG negative

mustNotMiss.note: Gynaecological mimics in a woman of reproductive age (secondary engine).
mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Web: Symptom inference top 5: appendicitis ×2, alcoholic pancreatitis, gastroenteritis, typhoid; no gynaecological cause for a 28-year-old woman.

mustInclude.note: Pregnancy test in every woman of reproductive age before imaging, drugs or theatre.
WSES 2020: ultrasound first in young women; CT if non-diagnostic.

WSES 2020 and CODA: antibiotics-first is a safe alternative for CT-confirmed uncomplicated appendicitis without appendicolith, after shared decision-making (about 3 in 10 need appendicectomy by 90 days).
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add a 'conservative' step to the appendicitis protocol: antibiotics-first for CT-confirmed uncomplicated appendicitis without appendicolith after shared decision (WSES 2020, CODA), with the recurrence figure.

guideline.name: WSES Jerusalem guidelines — diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis (2020 update)
guideline.section: Clinical scores (AIR/AAS over Alvarado), imaging by age/sex/pregnancy, antibiotic-first option, complicated appendicitis (abscess), antibiotic duration
guideline.citation: Di Saverio S, Podda M, De Simone B, et al. Diagnosis and treatment of acute appendicitis: 2020 update of the WSES Jerusalem guidelines. World J Emerg Surg. 2020;15:27.

guideline.name: CODA trial — antibiotics versus appendectomy for acute appendicitis
guideline.section: Non-inferiority of antibiotics-first for health status at 30 days; ~3 in 10 had appendicectomy by 90 days; appendicolith associated with more appendicectomies and complications
guideline.citation: CODA Collaborative. A randomized trial comparing antibiotics with appendectomy for appendicitis. N Engl J Med. 2020;383:1907–19.

guideline.name: Appendicitis Inflammatory Response (AIR) score
guideline.section: Items and weights; 0–4 low, 5–8 intermediate, 9–12 high probability
guideline.citation: Andersson M, Andersson RE. The appendicitis inflammatory response score: a tool for the diagnosis of acute appendicitis that outperforms the Alvarado score. World J Surg. 2008;32:1843–9.

rationale: Permutation: sex and treatment choice. Tests the pregnancy test, US-first imaging in a young woman, and whether the antibiotics-first option (WSES 2020, CODA) is offered alongside appendicectomy when the patient is eligible.
